Price comes from the server: map a product slug to its Stripe price in a table (or env var) and look it up in the flow, as the snippet does. A client-chosen `price_id` lets a buyer pay any price on the account. Grant the purchase from the verified webhook (`checkout.session.completed` with `payment_status` of `paid`), never from the success_url redirect.

Verify Stripe webhooks with the named provider check: `verify: stripe` plus `secret: "${{ env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET }}"` on the flow's on.request - see api(at:'webhooks') → inbound_example. `stripe_webhook_hmac` is an OUTBOUND `sign:` recipe, not a `verify:` recipe; the map form `verify: { recipe: … }` accepts only the recipes api(at:'verify') lists.
`benmore status` flags a LIVE key in dev or a TEST key in prod (payment-key preflight) - with Connect this can't happen, but BYO keys should be double-checked.

Disconnecting (dashboard → Payments) deauthorizes the platform at Stripe AND removes the env keys for that mode. Stripe's deauthorization covers the whole connected account, so when another app is still connected to the same account in that mode (disconnect or app delete) only this app's keys and connection are removed.

An ownership transfer does not carry the Connect connection: when the recipient accepts, each connection is removed from the app (its STRIPE_* keys in that mode's environment scope, the connection, and the grant at Stripe unless another app still uses the account), because it is the previous owner's Stripe account. It stays only when the new owner has already connected the same Stripe account on one of their own apps. Payments that used the connected keys fail until the new owner connects their own account; BYO keys set in another scope move with the rest of the environment.
